newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi Legislature overhauls school funding.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi Legislature overhauls school funding.

text.p: The Mississippi Senate has approved a $130 million overhaul of public education financing, legislative officials said.
The Mississippi Adequate Education Program (SB2649) passed 44-8 in the Senate Thursday, a day after clearing the House.
It was to be sent Friday to Gov. Kirk Fordice.
"He's not had an opportunity to look at it. He has not indicated one way or the other what his plans are," a Fordice spokeswoman said Friday.
If Fordice vetoes the proposal, the Legislature could not vote on an override until the 1998 session.
Mississippi is one of many states struggling to achieve funding equity in public schools. Unlike other states, its proposed solution would not require wealthier districts to pay more.

Instead, it would use general fund surpluses and new revenues from economic growth to infuse poor districts with additional money. Fueled by casino gambling, Mississippi has enjoyed record budget surpluses in the 1990s.
The proposal would increase overall school spending by $12 million to $14 million annually, giving every county an eight percent increase as the program is phased in over six years.
The bill calls for establishment of a state minimum for per-student spending, to be determined by the average per-pupil cost in districts recognized for high achievement.
Districts whose spending fall below that level will be subsidized by the state, using a formula based on local tax contributions, student population and the number of at-risk students.
